clue.text: Footballers confronting old rebel make an appearance

parts.note: FA, the Football Association, the body governing English footballers
Jack Cade led a rebellion in Kent in 1450

explanation.surface: Footballers face up to an old rebel when they turn out for a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confronting' means facing, so the footballers go in front. Jack Cade led a peasants' revolt in Kent in 1450, which makes him the old rebel.
explanation.definitionFit: A facade is the outward show a thing presents, its exterior look.

clue.text: They shed light on Pam's golf playing

indicators.note: playing here means acting up or behaving loosely, so the letters of the phrase are rearranged

explanation.surface: Lamps help us see how Pam plays her golf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing' rearranges PAMSGOLF (the S of the possessive counts).
explanation.definitionFit: Fog lamps are bright car lights for poor visibility.

clue.text: Vehicles fore and aft of a camel train

parts.note: a car is one vehicle
a van is another vehicle

explanation.surface: Wagons positioned at the front and back of a line of camels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fore and aft of' places one vehicle in front of A and another behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: A caravan is a group of travellers with pack animals crossing a desert together.

clue.text: Channel port only producing fish

parts.note: Dover is a port on the English Channel
sole means only, as in sole survivor

explanation.surface: A harbour town on the Channel that turns out nothing but fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Dover sole is a prized flatfish of European waters.

clue.text: Holiday taken when twenty-weeks pregnant?

parts.note: a pregnancy runs to full term at about forty weeks, so twenty weeks is midway; the real sense is a school break in the middle of a term

explanation.surface: A mother-to-be takes a break when she is twenty weeks along.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a school year has three terms, each split by a week's break in the middle; the clue puns on 'term' as the length of a pregnancy.
explanation.definitionFit: A school's mid-term break is a short holiday for pupils and teachers.

clue.text: Finished the purchasing in state of confusion

parts.note: all over means completely finished
to shop is to purchase goods

explanation.surface: Done with the shopping, and in a muddle.
explanation.definitionFit: All over the shop is an idiom for disorganised or scattered everywhere.

clue.text: Study by leading fellow displays talent

indicators.note: leading picks out the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: a study or den is a lair, a private retreat

explanation.surface: A top fellow's study shows his gifts.
explanation.definitionFit: Flair is a natural aptitude or knack.

clue.text: It's clear I have been upset by depression

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the contracted words are read backwards

parts.note: I have contracts to I've
a dent is a hollow or depression

explanation.surface: Clearly I have been knocked back by feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' turns I'VE into EVI; 'depression' looks emotional but is a dent.
explanation.definitionFit: Evident means plain to see, obvious.

clue.text: Distress call made on workers' holiday

explanation.surface: An SOS sent out on Labour Day.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayday is the radio signal for an emergency, and May Day is the 1 May labour festival.

clue.text: Coming timetable to delight children before Christmas

parts.note: advent means a coming or arrival
a calendar is a schedule of dates

explanation.surface: A schedule of what's coming, to thrill youngsters in December.
explanation.definitionFit: Children open a door each day in December on this card or box, finding a picture or chocolate.

clue.text: Us novelist who drove Gail crazy

indicators.note: crazy says the letters of the two words go wild and are rearranged

explanation.surface: An American writer once drove a woman named Gail out of her mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crazy' rearranges DROVE GAIL. 'Us' is printed without its stops; read it as US, the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Gore Vidal was an American author of novels such as Burr and Myra Breckinridge.

clue.text: Goodwill displayed by woman without sex appeal

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the woman's name wraps round the other piece

parts.note: Amy is a woman's name
IT is a long-standing slang word for sex appeal

explanation.surface: Kindness is shown by a woman who lacks allure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but here it has its old sense of 'outside', so the woman's name goes round the slang word for sex appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Amity is friendly relations, a state of peace and friendship.

clue.text: Dire commercial jingle

parts.note: an ad is a commercial
a jingle is a piece of light verse

explanation.surface: A terrible advertising tune.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverse conditions are harmful or unfavourable, close to dire.

clue.text: Beaver resolved to consume new plant

indicators.note: to consume means to take in, so the rearranged letters swallow the other piece
resolved in the sense of broken down and re-formed, so the letters of the animal are rearranged

explanation.surface: A beaver is determined to eat a fresh plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resolved' rearranges BEAVER to VERBEA, and 'to consume' puts N inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Verbena is a garden flower, also called vervain.

clue.text: Penny gets interested in a horse

parts.note: to be into something is to be keen on it

explanation.surface: Penny takes up an interest in a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penny' reads as a girl's name but gives P.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinto is a piebald or skewbald horse with patchy markings.

clue.text: Floods causing fissure in hills

indicators.note: in places the crack inside the word for the hills

parts.note: tors are rocky hills, as on Dartmoor
a rent is a split or tear

explanation.surface: Floods open up a crack in the hillside.
explanation.definitionFit: Torrents are rushing streams of water, deluges.

clue.text: A lightning-conductor?

parts.note: read literally, a thing that conducts electric current, as a terminal in a battery or valve does

explanation.surface: A rod on a roof to carry strikes to earth.
explanation.walkthrough: The rod on a steeple is the false trail; think of any part that conducts electricity.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrode is a conductor through which current enters or leaves a circuit.

clue.text: I get rebuked about note being repeated

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the pair of words goes round the musical note

parts.note: to rate is an old word for to scold
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: I am told off over a note that I keep playing again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'concerning', but it means 'around': the note sits inside 'I rated', with RATE as an old word for scold.
explanation.definitionFit: Iterated means said or done again.

clue.text: Way to keep pitheads repaired

indicators.note: repaired means put back together, so these letters are fixed in a new order

explanation.surface: A route maintained so that the mine's pitheads are kept in good order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repaired' rearranges PITHEADS; 'to keep' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A side path is a minor track or footpath leading off a main route.

clue.text: Picture published by one journal in the Orient

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
mag is short for magazine, a journal
E stands for east, the Orient

explanation.surface: An image printed by a single magazine in the Far East.
explanation.definitionFit: To imagine is to form a mental image of something.

clue.text: Old law is quite precise

parts.note: EX- means former or old
an act is a law passed by parliament

explanation.surface: An ancient statute is very exact in its wording.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact means accurate in every detail, entirely correct.

clue.text: The first male worker is uncompromising

parts.note: Adam was the first man in Genesis
a worker ant

explanation.surface: The original man, a labourer, will not give an inch.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamant means unyielding and inflexible.

clue.text: Gently waters bunches of flowers

explanation.surface: A gardener lightly waters the posies.
explanation.definitionFit: To spray is to sprinkle with a fine mist, and sprays are small floral arrangements.

clue.text: Appease a top copper investing in silver

indicators.note: investing in means going inside, so the two letters sit within the word for silver

parts.note: plate is household silver

indicators.note: top picks the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Calm down a senior police officer who has put money into silver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top copper' looks like a chief of police, but 'top' takes C from 'copper'; A and C then go inside PLATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To placate someone is to pacify or soothe them.

clue.text: Stop a minister returning on time

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the cleric's abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a minister

explanation.surface: A minister heads back on time to prevent something.
explanation.definitionFit: To avert is to prevent or ward off.

clue.text: Group of average ability likely to succeed

parts.note: a set is a group
fair means middling, neither good nor bad

explanation.surface: A team of middling talent is tipped to do well.
explanation.definitionFit: Set fair, first said of settled weather, means well placed for a good outcome.

clue.text: Alert doughboy gets stuck into the drink

indicators.note: gets stuck into puts the soldier inside the word for the drink

parts.note: ale is a drink
doughboy is old slang for an American infantryman, a GI

explanation.surface: A wide-awake soldier starts on his beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doughboy' was a nickname for an American soldier in the First World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Agile can mean quick-witted and sharp, mentally nimble.

clue.text: Air-freshener not adored in any way

indicators.note: in any way says the letters may be arranged any old how

explanation.surface: An air-freshener that nobody likes at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A deodorant masks bad smells, as a spray or stick does.

clue.text: Realise celebrities are affected by flashing lights

parts.note: to see is to realise or understand
stars are celebrities

explanation.surface: Famous people realise they are dazzled by camera flashes.
explanation.definitionFit: To see stars is to have flashes before the eyes, as after a blow to the head.

clue.text: Ran furiously, yet got beaten

explanation.surface: A runner sprinted all out and still lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Belted means raced at top speed, and also thrashed with a strap.
